payload.body: The AC-1/AC-2 integration regression (harness process holds an open OS pipe as its own stdin, imports parrot which installs uvloop, then calls the REAL production CodexCodeDispatcher._create_process() via uvloop.run() to spawn a grandchild) fails 100% reproducibly when run inside this repo's full pytest session (packages/ai-parrot/tests/flows/dev_loop/), even after 3 retries — the grandchild's fd0 was verified via /proc/<pid>/fd to be the harness's own stdin pipe inode, not /dev/null, despite _create_process() correctly passing stdin=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL (verified independently and deterministically by test_spawn_isolates_stdin in the same file). The identical harness+child scripts, spawned the identical way (stdlib subprocess.Popen, close_fds=True), pass reliably every time when run as a standalone script OUTSIDE pytest (multiple confirmed reproductions). The harness's own /proc/<pid>/fd table shows 2 extra open sockets present only in the pytest-driven run that do not appear in the standalone reproduction, despite close_fds=True on the Popen call, suggesting the full pytest session's accumulated process state affects a subsequent fork+exec's fd landscape in a way that trips a libuv/uvloop 0.21.0 subprocess-spawn DEVNULL-handling bug. This is not a defect in _create_process() or the hotfix; suggested follow-up: reproduce with a minimal pytest fixture set to bisect which conftest.py fixture/import introduces the extra descriptors, or file upstream against uvloop with a minimal repro, or accept a documented xfail/skip for this one test in CI while relying on test_spawn_isolates_stdin (deterministic mock) for the DEVNULL-kwarg contract.

The identical harness+child scripts, spawned the identical way (stdlib subprocess.Popen, close_fds=True), pass reliably every time when run as a standalone script OUTSIDE pytest (multiple confirmed reproductions). The harness's own /proc/<pid>/fd table shows 2 extra open sockets present only in the pytest-driven run that do not appear in the standalone reproduction, despite close_fds=True on the Popen call, suggesting the full pytest session's accumulated process state affects a subsequent fork+exec's fd landscape in a way that trips a libuv/uvloop 0.21.0 subprocess-spawn DEVNULL-handling bug. This is not a defect in _create_process() or the hotfix; suggested follow-up: reproduce with a minimal pytest fixture set to bisect which conftest.py fixture/import introduces the extra descriptors, or file upstream against uvloop with a minimal repro, or accept a documented xfail/skip for this one test in CI while relying on test_spawn_isolates_stdin (deterministic mock) for the DEVNULL-kwarg contract.

sdd-coder: no nova MCP seat is eligible for 'unknown'-classified tasks, no fallback to native/codex-spark
payload.body:
coder_plan assigns unknown-classified tasks (metric_unknown reason code, e.g. because
wiki_blast_radius exits 1 for their contract_symbols) to standard nova MCP seats
(glm/mistral/qwen/minimax/glm5), but coder_run_chunk's dispatch-time eligibility check
rejects every one of them with:
  CoderFailure: seat '<label>' (backend='nova', model='<model>') is not eligible for
  unknown task TASK-<NNN>

Reproduced deterministically on FEAT-572 (sdd-fix-ledger-lane) across 3 independent
coder_plan/coder_run_chunk cycles for TASK-3393, TASK-3396, TASK-3397 (all classification
"unknown"): every one of the 5 configured nova seats (glm, mistral, qwen, minimax, glm5)
was tried at least once and rejected with the identical eligibility error; each task's
2-attempt retry rotation never included the native (haiku/sonnet) or codex-spark seats,
which ARE eligible per the planner's own docstring ("complex/unknown tasks are restricted
to strong-model seats"). coder_prepare_native also refuses to adopt these tasks
(error.code=task_not_in_plan) because the plan never assigned them a native seat in the
first place - there is no operator-side workaround; the tasks are permanently stuck.

Impact: any task whose complexity assessment lands on "unknown" (e.g. because the wiki's
blast-radius collector errors out, which happens routinely - blast_symbols state=unknown
appeared on 7 of the 12 tasks assessed in this same feature) can never be dispatched to
any of the 5 nova seats, and the planner never routes it to a seat that would accept it.

Suggested fix: either (a) the planner's chunk-seat assignment must only ever assign an
"unknown"/"complex" task to a seat from the eligible set (native sonnet/haiku or
codex-spark), never to a standard nova seat as chunk-time is currently doing, or (b) the
dispatch-time retry rotation for a rejected "unknown" task must include the eligible
seats instead of cycling through the same ineligible nova pool.

Evidence: coder_wait job-00cdece6c00d, job-1677572b6ba3 (attempts[].error field, this
worktree feat-FEAT-572-sdd-fix-ledger-lane, execution_id
270ef7d3-edc6-48e4-b304-6179e72bd4d7).

codex sdd-coder seats can never commit: codex's workspace-write sandbox keeps .git read-only, so every codex attempt ends as dirty_task_worktree
payload.body:
## Finding

A `codex`-backed sdd-coder seat cannot `git commit`. `CodexCodeDispatcher` runs
`codex exec --cd <worktree> --sandbox workspace-write` (codex.py:450-468), and that sandbox keeps
`.git` **read-only**. The coder writes its files, passes lint, returns a clean `DevelopmentOutput`
with `commit_shas: []` — and `_consolidate` (engine.py:1517) then sees a dirty tree and fails the
attempt with `dirty_task_worktree`.

This is the real root cause of the recurring "complex task fails, then complex_model_unavailable"
pattern (see [[issue:569e81756247]]): attempt 1 on the codex strong seat `gpt-5.6-terra` can never
commit, so it always fails, and the retry ladder then has nowhere to go.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-09-21, codex-cli 0.155.1)

In a linked worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`:

```
codex exec --sandbox workspace-write -c 'approval_policy="never"' \
  'Run: git add -A && git commit -m probe'
→ fatal: Unable to create '<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>/index.lock': Read-only file system
```

Neither remedy works: `-c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["<repo>/.git"]'` and
`--add-dir <repo>/.git` both give the same error. `--add-dir` itself is fine
(`--add-dir /tmp/probe` + `touch /tmp/probe/ok.txt` succeeds), so `.git` is specifically protected
by codex, not a flag problem.

## Live evidence

TASK-3565 (FEAT-584) attempt worktree `...--pool/TASK-3565-a1-d4a1d075d068474fa254201190e68fa8`
holds 3 modified-but-uncommitted files with HEAD still on the prior task's commit — exactly this
signature. A full replay of TASK-3549 on `codex/gpt-5.6-luna` reproduced it end to end: a complete
298-line `scripts/sdd/worktree_status.py`, ruff clean, then *"commit was blocked because the shared
git admin directory is read-only"*.

The engine cannot rescue this: its only commit is the lint autofix (lint.py:159), which runs after
`_consolidate`'s dirty-tree check already failed the attempt.

## Scope

Every `codex` seat: standard-tier `codex-spark` and both strong seats `gpt-5.6-terra` and
`gpt-5.6-luna` (the latter added as a mitigation for [[issue:569e81756247]] — that mitigation is
therefore ineffective, both hops being codex). Probably unaffected, to be probe-confirmed:
in-process backends (`nova`, `google-compat`), whose tools run inside the parrot process with no CLI
sandbox, and native Claude seats, whose bubblewrap policy explicitly makes Git metadata writable
(`.claude/rules/worktree-management.md` §4). `google_coding` is separately blocked by
[[issue:e7bdce192812]]; whether `agy --sandbox` also protects `.git` is untested.

## Candidate fixes

1. Have the engine commit the coder's declared files when the tree is dirty but fidelity-clean.
   Makes every CLI backend's sandbox policy irrelevant; the only option that weakens no sandbox.
2. Dispatch coder attempts with `--sandbox danger-full-access`, relying on the worktree bubblewrap
   isolation already wrapping these runs. Weakens defence in depth — needs a deliberate decision.
3. Give each attempt sub-worktree a self-contained gitdir so `.git` is a real directory inside cwd.
   Useless if codex protects `.git` by name regardless of location — test first.

Whichever is chosen, add a probe assertion that a seat can actually produce a commit, so a backend
that structurally cannot deliver is rejected at `coder_begin_execution` rather than after burning a
full attempt on every task.

payload.body:
Supersedes and reframes `issue:c4d0e7a028ca`, which wrongly blamed codex. **Design decision
(Jesus, 2026-09-21):** under the bubblewrap/sandbox policy a coder seat's `.git` is deliberately
read-only. A coder is *not* supposed to commit. Producing the commit is the orchestrator's job —
`sdd-worker` / `SddCoderEngine`, which run outside the sandbox, extract the coder's work from the
attempt worktree and commit it. See `mem-c163c2dde8ff`.

## The defect

`SddCoderEngine._consolidate` (engine.py:1516-1526) still opens with a clean-tree requirement:
`git status --porcelain -uall` non-empty ⇒ `dirty_task_worktree`, attempt failed. That contradicts
the design: it fails precisely the attempts that behaved correctly. A sandboxed seat delivers the
work in the tree and cannot commit it, so the engine throws away good work.

Backend-independent. Not "codex cannot commit" — no sandboxed seat is meant to. Seats that do
commit today (native Claude, in-process nova/google-compat) merely happen to hold write access; they
are the exception, not the model to copy.

## Rejected approaches

- Dispatching with `--sandbox danger-full-access`, or `--add-dir`/`writable_roots` onto `.git`:
  deliberately defeats the sandbox policy.
- Giving each attempt sub-worktree a self-contained gitdir inside cwd: exists only to hand the coder
  git write access. Same objection.

## Required behaviour

In `_consolidate`, before the fidelity gate, when the tree is dirty:

1. Stage only the task's **declared** files — `parse_task_files(task_md)`, the same `expected` set
   `check_fidelity` already uses (engine.py:1554). Never `DevelopmentOutput.files_changed`, which is
   coder-reported and would let a seat widen its own scope. Never a `sdd/` path.
2. Commit them on the attempt branch (the engine already commits here — `run_lint_pass` does exactly
   this at lint.py:159 — so no new capability is needed).
3. Re-check `git status`. Anything still dirty is an undeclared file the coder produced: report it as
   `unexpected_files` / `fidelity_violation`, never silently drop or commit it.
4. No-op when the tree is already clean, so native and in-process seats are unaffected.

The fidelity gate then runs on the committed diff exactly as today and gets *stronger*: scope is
enforced by what the engine chooses to stage, not by what the coder chose to commit.

## Knock-on decisions

- `dirty_task_worktree` is currently a retryable error class (engine.py:2262, 2540-2554). Once the
  engine commits, that retry path stops firing for sandboxed seats; confirm nothing else depends on
  it before removing.
- `DevelopmentOutput.commit_shas` will be empty for these attempts. Audit consumers.
- Add a probe/test asserting an attempt whose tree is dirty-but-declared consolidates successfully.

## Evidence this is throwing away good work

Replay of TASK-3549 on `codex/gpt-5.6-luna`: the seat produced a complete
`scripts/sdd/worktree_status.py`, ruff-clean, and reported the commit blocked by the read-only git
dir. Scored against the era-correct TASK-3550 test suite it passed **22/22**, while the original
committed delivery of the same task passed only 18/22. Under current `_consolidate` that attempt is
discarded as `dirty_task_worktree`.

payload.body: DetectionBox (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/models/detections.py:37-56) declares class_id: int, class_name: str, area: int with default=None but WITHOUT Optional[...] typing. A plain model_dump_json() on any DetectionBox (or a model containing one, e.g. PerceptionResult) writes an explicit null for these three fields when they were never set. payload.title: end_execution's snapshot-enrichment loop constructs an invalid AttemptRecord as a dict.get default
payload.body: engine.py's end_execution() snapshot-enrichment loop (introduced by TASK-3282) has: manager_key = f"{task_id}.a{self._latest_attempt.get(task_id, AttemptRecord(attempt=1)).attempt}". payload.title: GoogleCodingDispatcher writes its --json-schema to the host /tmp, which agy --sandbox cannot read — the google_coding seat fails every dispatch
payload.body:
## Symptom

Every `google_coding` (agy) dispatch fails immediately, before the model runs:

```
DispatchExecutionError: agy CLI dispatch failed with exit code 1:
Error: invalid --json-schema: failed to read schema file
"/tmp/dev_loop_agy_schema_so0wy9ca.json": open ...: no such file or directory
```

Fails in ~0.2s with exit code 1. The file *does* exist on the host at that moment — it is unlinked
only in the `finally` at google_coding.py:281-286.

## Root cause

`GoogleCodingDispatcher._materialize_json_schema` (google_coding.py:361-373) uses
`tempfile.mkstemp()`, i.e. the host temp dir. `GoogleCodingDispatchProfile.sandbox` defaults to
`True` (models/google_coding.py:29), and `_build_command` passes `--sandbox` (google_coding.py:311).
`agy --sandbox` runs with a **private /tmp**, so a host temp path is not visible inside it. The
schema path is the only argument pointing outside the workspace.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-09-21, agy 1.2.0)

Run from a worktree under `WORKTREE_BASE_PATH`:

- `agy --json-schema /tmp/probe.json --output-format json --sandbox --print='...'`
  → `failed to read schema file ... no such file or directory`
- `agy --json-schema .probe.json --output-format json --sandbox --print='...'`
  (identical file, inside cwd) → `"status":"SUCCESS"` with a correct `structured_output` object.

Only the schema's location differs.

## Impact

The `google_coding` backend is unusable as an sdd-coder seat today. It is silently masked: the
`RosterProbe` smoke call fails the same way, so the seat is dropped as "unavailable" and looks like a
credentials/CLI problem rather than a dispatcher bug. `sdd/state/FEAT-549/design_research/open_questions.txt`
records the agy fallback validation as never executed, which is why this survived.

## Proposed fix

Materialize the schema **inside `cwd`** rather than the host temp dir, and keep the existing `finally`
unlink.

Care is needed on placement: an untracked leftover in the worktree root would make
`SddCoderEngine._consolidate` (engine.py:1517, `git status --porcelain -uall`) report
`dirty_task_worktree` and fail an otherwise-good attempt if the process is killed before cleanup.
Write it somewhere `git status` does not see — e.g. under the worktree's git dir, or a path already
ignored — rather than a bare dotfile in the worktree root.

Add a regression test asserting the schema path passed to `--json-schema` is under `cwd`
(packages/ai-parrot/tests/flows/dev_loop/test_google_coding_dispatcher.py).

## Related

Discovered while validating `gemini-3.8-flash-high` as a second strong MCP seat for
[[issue:569e81756247]] (complex tasks get zero retries). That seat had to fall back to
codex/`gpt-5.6-luna` because of this bug. Note also that agy model ids are effort-suffixed
(`gemini-3.8-flash-high`); a bare `gemini-3.8-flash` is not a valid id, and
`parrot/flows/dev_loop/catalog.py`'s `google_coding` models tuple lists bare, stale names
(`gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini-3.0-pro`).

payload.title: review_checkpoint prepare always fails checkpoint_busy after any coder_run_chunk dispatch
payload.body: CoderEngine._job_worktrees (engine.py:383) records job_id -> worktree at dispatch time (line 3588) and is NEVER pruned anywhere in the file (verified: only 2 write sites, both additive; grep for del/pop finds none). end_execution's snapshot enrichment (engine.py:859-861) unconditionally copies EVERY job_id in _job_worktrees matching the closing worktree into snapshot.outstanding_job_ids, with no check of the job's actual terminal state. review_checkpoint.prepare_review_checkpoint (checkpoint.py:483-489) then treats any non-empty outstanding_job_ids as CheckpointBusyError, unconditionally. Net effect: once a worktree has dispatched at least one coder_run_chunk job in the engine process's lifetime, coder_end_execution's own published settlement snapshot can NEVER have an empty outstanding_job_ids, so 'python -m scripts.sdd.review_checkpoint prepare' permanently fails with checkpoint_busy for that worktree, even when every job is independently confirmed state=done/outcome=completed via coder_wait/coder_status (reproduced on FEAT-592: 4 jobs, all coder_status-verified done, coder_end_execution returned status=closed, yet review_checkpoint prepare reported '4 job(s)' outstanding). Suggested fix: only append a job_id to outstanding_job_ids when its recorded state is not a terminal one (running/unknown), or remove/mark job_ids from _job_worktrees once coder_wait/coder_status observes a terminal state.

payload.title: coder_end_execution never clears _job_worktrees, permanently blocking review_checkpoint prepare
payload.body: SddCoderEngine._job_worktrees (engine.py:383) is set once per dispatched coder_run_chunk job (engine.py:3588, self._job_worktrees[job.job_id] = ctx.worktree) and is never deleted anywhere in the module (grep confirms only 4 references: init, set, and two read-only enumerations). coder_end_execution's snapshot enrichment (engine.py:859-862) unconditionally appends every job_id in _job_worktrees whose worktree matches the closing execution's worktree_path into the durable ExecutionSnapshot.outstanding_job_ids, regardless of whether coder_status/coder_wait already reported that job's state as 'done'. The gate at engine.py:839 that is supposed to refuse close on outstanding jobs reads pool.snapshot() BEFORE this enrichment (pool.py:207/219 shows native_reservations/outstanding_job_ids are intentionally empty at that layer), so the gate is a no-op and end_execution always reports status='closed' even with stale job ids present. scripts/sdd/review_checkpoint.py's prepare_review_checkpoint (checkpoint.py:472-489) then reads that persisted, polluted snapshot and correctly refuses with checkpoint_busy ('N job(s)') for every execution that ever ran coder_run_chunk at least once -- observed live on FEAT-591 execution a3f1c2e4-7b6d-4a89-9e0f-2c8d5b4a1f37: job-2ecb8c316215 (coder_run_chunk for TASK-3623) completed cleanly per coder_status (state=done, all tasks merged) at 13:16:00Z, coder_end_execution succeeded ~13:26Z, yet review_checkpoint prepare still reports '0 attempt(s), 0 reservation(s), 1 job(s)' outstanding, permanently blocking the FEAT-584 M8 review-checkpoint step described in the sdd-worker Completion protocol for any feature whose worker used the MCP dispatch path at all. Suggested fix: pop the job_id from self._job_worktrees once its terminal state is durably observed (e.g. in status()/wait() when job.state == 'done', or filter outstanding_job_ids in the enrichment loop to jobs whose self._jobs[job_id].state != 'done').

schema sync crashes for postgres/bigquery: duplicate database_type kwarg in toolkit_for()
payload.body:
producers/live.py:34-41 `toolkit_for()` always passes `database_type=cfg.dialect` when constructing the dialect toolkit. `PostgresToolkit.__init__` (toolkits/postgres.py:98-108) and `BigQueryToolkit.__init__` (toolkits/bigquery.py:42-49) both already hardcode `database_type="postgresql"`/`"bigquery"` in their own `super().__init__(...)` call and accept `**kwargs` (they do NOT declare `database_type` as a named param), so the caller's `database_type=cfg.dialect` kwarg flows through `**kwargs` and collides with the hardcoded one, raising `TypeError: __init__() got multiple values for keyword argument 'database_type'`.

Impact: `wikitoolkit schema sync <origin>` crashes for any postgres or bigquery source — the two primary supported dialects, and the exact scenario used in the spec's own AC1 worked example (`--dialect bigquery`). Only the `SQLToolkit` fallback path (e.g. sqlite) works. This breaks AC2 (sync creates pages) and AC1's worked example for the two dialects that matter most in production.

Confirmed by: `packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/wiki/schema/test_live_producer.py::test_toolkit_choice[postgres-PostgresToolkit]` and `[bigquery-BigQueryToolkit]` both fail with this exact TypeError; verified independently by reading toolkits/postgres.py:98-108 and toolkits/bigquery.py:42-49.

Suggested fix: `toolkit_for()` should only pass `database_type=cfg.dialect` to the generic `SQLToolkit` fallback branch, not to dialect-specific subclasses that already set it internally (e.g. omit the kwarg when `toolkit_class is not SQLToolkit`).

payload.title: Post-merge hook's `schema ingest-ddl --changed --quiet` always fails (missing required --origin/--dialect)
payload.body:
claude_code/assets.py:193 (git_hook_block) adds `{wt_bin} schema ingest-ddl --changed --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` inside the `if [ ! -f .git ]` guard — placement is correct per AC10, but the command itself always fails. `schema_ingest_ddl` in cli.py declares `--origin` and `--dialect` as `required=True` click options (cli.py:3193-3194) with no fallback that loops over `schema.sources` in config when omitted. Running the exact hook invocation through Click's CliRunner immediately fails at argument parsing with `Error: Missing option '--origin'.` (SystemExit 2).

Because the hook wraps the call in `|| true`, the hook script itself never breaks, but the automated DDL-drift capture on every merge (the entire point of wiring this into the git hook) silently never runs — it is a permanent no-op. `test_schema_hook_assets.py::test_ingest_line_inside_guard` only string-checks placement and never exercises the command, so this gap is untested and unnoticed.

Suggested fix: either give `schema ingest-ddl` a mode that loops over all declared `schema.sources` (deriving origin+dialect from config) when `--origin`/`--dialect` are omitted with `--changed`, or have the hook line itself loop over configured origins.

payload.title: BasicAgent.__init__ unconditionally constructs GoogleGenAIClient regardless of llm=
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/bots/agent.py:114-116 does `from ..clients.google import GoogleGenAIClient` then `default_client = GoogleGenAIClient()` on EVERY BasicAgent construction, before checking self._llm_raw. So constructing BasicAgent(name=..., llm='anthropic:...') still imports and instantiates the Google client; when google-genai / the ai-parrot-client-google satellite is not importable, construction raises ImportError/instantiation error even though Google was never requested. The comment claims a lazy import to avoid module-scope provider imports (AC-3), but it is still unconditional at __init__ time. Fix: only construct the Google default client when it is actually the resolved provider (or lazily on first multimodal/TTS use). Discovered while wiring FEAT-586's hello-world (test_hello_world_snippet_executes had to inject a fake parrot.clients.google to construct BasicAgent).

payload.title: hooba: AC-17 no-real-data scan filter discards every match found inside tests/hooba itself
payload.body: test_no_real_data_committed (packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/hooba/test_integration_e2e.py:111-146) git-greps both packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/hooba and packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/hooba for forbidden patterns (real HOOBA_PASSWORD, Spanish IBAN, real session id), then filters matches with `if "test" not in line.lower() and "fixture" not in line.lower()`. Since every git-grep hit from the tests/hooba path naturally contains "test" in its own file path (e.g. "tests/hooba/..."), this filter discards 100% of matches originating from the tests directory -- the exact directory the scan is supposed to police for accidentally-committed real credentials/PII (per AC-17). A real leaked credential inside a test fixture would never be caught by this check. Suggested fix: filter on the matched line's content only (not the git-grep-prefixed file path), or scope the "test"/"fixture" exclusion to known synthetic-fixture markers rather than the substring "test" which is unavoidably present in every tests/hooba path.

payload.title: hooba: auto_open's login gate makes hooba_recover_web_session unreachable exactly when API auth is broken
payload.body: HoobaToolkit.auto_open = True (toolkit.py:73), and AbstractToolkit's ToolkitTool._execute path runs `await toolkit._ensure_open()` (which calls HoobaToolkit._open() -> self._api._ensure_session(), i.e. the API login_hook) BEFORE any tool's own body runs (parrot/tools/toolkit.py:166-169), including hooba_recover_web_session's own body. hooba_recover_web_session's entire purpose (per its docstring: "Recover a browser session and inject its sid cookie into the API jar") is to recover from a broken/expired API-cookie session via the Playwright browser fallback. But because _ensure_open() raises before the tool body runs when the API login itself is failing, the one tool designed to recover from that exact failure can never be invoked to do its job -- the auto_open gate blocks it upstream. Suggested fix: add "hooba_recover_web_session" to HoobaToolkit.exclude_tools' sibling mechanism or otherwise exempt it from the auto_open gate (e.g. a toolkit-level override, or catching the open failure specifically for this one recovery tool), so it can still run when the API session is broken.

payload.title: hooba: (name, price) line-dedup signature can silently drop legitimate duplicate lines
payload.body: _line_signature (packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/hooba/toolkit.py:463-466) builds a (name, price) tuple used by _sync_lines_and_finalize to decide whether a line already exists on a reused draft (skip re-posting it). Two genuinely distinct line items that happen to share the same name and price (a realistic case: two identical-priced products, e.g. "Consulting hour" x2 at different times, or two identical expense lines on a BBVA-derived purchase invoice) collapse to the same signature -- the second legitimate line is silently treated as "already present" and never posted, permanently losing it from the draft on any resume/retry. Suggested fix: include quantity (or a stable per-line ordinal/index) in the signature, or track posted-line identity via something more specific than (name, price) alone.

payload.title: hooba: BBVA row-count cross-check's ExcelLoader.load() call is not offloaded off the event loop
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/hooba/bank/bbva.py:207-213 -- the independent row-count cross-check (S10) constructs an ExcelLoader and awaits its .load() call directly inside the async parse_bbva_statement path, without wrapping the (openpyxl-backed, disk-bound) load in asyncio.to_thread. This partially violates AC-11's "parses off the event loop" requirement and the repo's async-first convention (never block the event loop in async def). The primary BBVA parse path itself (_parse_bbva_sync) is correctly offloaded; only this secondary cross-check call is not. Suggested fix: wrap the ExcelLoader construction+load in asyncio.to_thread, matching the primary parse path's pattern.

payload.title: hooba: BBVA checkpoint manifest path is not scoped by Hooba account
payload.body: manifest_path_for(digest) (packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/hooba/bank/manifest.py:29-31) keys the per-statement checkpoint manifest ONLY by the statement's content digest: `$PARROT_STATE_DIR/business_automation/checkpoints/hooba_bbva_import/<digest>.manifest.json` -- there is no account/tenant component in the path. Two different Hooba accounts (e.g. two client deployments sharing one $PARROT_STATE_DIR, or a dev/staging split) that happen to import statements with byte-identical content would collide on the same manifest file, corrupting each other's resume/reconcile state. Low likelihood in practice (the digest already covers real banking data, unlikely to collide across genuinely different accounts) but a real architectural gap given the toolkit is explicitly multi-account-capable (accountId is resolved per HoobaSettings/credential). Suggested fix: include the resolved accountId (or credential_user_id) as a path segment/prefix alongside the digest.
